Getting started with decideR

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(decideR)

Why

An agronomist closing out a nitrogen trial holds posterior draws of grain yield at a handful of candidate rates and one concrete question to answer for the grower: what rate should go on, and how much should I trust that number? decideR answers both halves of that question with one call: it turns a posterior into the profit-maximising rate over the candidates on offer, and it declines to recommend a rate at all when the yield evidence behind the posterior has not been checked against its source. This vignette walks that nitrogen decision from posterior draws to a marked-up candidate curve, shows the refusal for real on the identical draws, and then carries the same engine into two further settings – a trading position sized under a capital-preservation constraint, and a grain-quality payoff that steps rather than rises smoothly – because the underlying question, act under uncertainty or decline to, is the same question in every one of them.

What

decide() is the shared keystone every decision in this vignette reduces to. Given posterior draws of a latent state, a utility(action, theta) function, and a set of candidate actions, it evaluates the expected utility of each feasible candidate by averaging over the draws and returns a decision: an S7 object carrying the chosen action, the expected_utility that justified it, the full candidates ledger, and two fields the Independent Oracle Principle requires on every decision – grounding and the abstention record (abstained, abstain_reason). A decision abstains, in priority order, when the combined grounding is not grounded, when no candidate is feasible, when the effective sample size falls below an opt-in min_ess floor, or when the leading candidate does not clearly beat the safe action; a fifth trigger catches a utility that returns no usable value anywhere on the grid. grounding_grounded() and grounding_unverified() are the two tokens a fact can carry, and combine_grounding() folds several into one worst case, so a decision resting on several inputs is only as grounded as its weakest one. The full vocabulary of abstention reasons, in the order decide() checks them:

The abstention vocabulary decide() reports, checked in order.
Reason Meaning
input_ungrounded An input fact carries grounding_unverified() (the IOP firewall).
no_feasible_action No candidate satisfies the feasibility constraint.
low_ess The effective sample size is below min_ess (opt-in; off by default).
insufficient_evidence The best action does not clearly beat the safe action.
degenerate_utility Every feasible candidate’s expected utility is NA or NaN.

decide_input_rate() and decide_position_size() are the two reference decisions this vignette exercises directly: the first chooses an agronomic input rate by expected profit over a matrix of per-rate yield draws, the second sizes a trading position by capped expected log-growth (the Kelly objective) under a hard one-period loss-quantile constraint. Both route through decide()’s shared core, so a nitrogen rate and a trading position are, structurally, the same computation with a different utility and a different candidate grid. decide_from_manifest() and its agronomic convenience decide_rate_from_manifest() are the manifest-native pipeline tail: given an orchestra_manifest (or any S7 object exposing the same outputs/metadata/summary properties) emitted upstream, they read the predictive draws and the producer’s own grounding token straight off it, so a decision at the end of a pipeline never re-derives provenance an upstream member already established. grade_band_value() builds a step value schedule for a quality-graded payoff – a grain price that jumps at a threshold rather than rising continuously – and grade_band_utility() turns that schedule into a decide() utility directly (not exercised below, where the equivalent shift is written by hand to keep the worked example self-contained).

Do

A nitrogen-rate decision

An upstream model – a mechanistic-simulator inversion, say – has produced posterior draws of grain yield at each of a set of candidate nitrogen rates, following a diminishing-returns response with posterior noise. The engine chooses the rate that maximises expected profit, E[pyy(r)−prr]\mathrm{E}[p_y\,y(r) - p_r\,r], at a grain price pyp_y and an input price prp_r.

rates <- seq(0, 200, by = 25)
ymax <- rnorm(2000L, mean = 5.5, sd = 0.3)      # posterior of asymptotic yield
yield_draws <- vapply(
  rates,
  function(r) 3 + (ymax - 3) * (1 - exp(-r / 80)) + rnorm(2000L, 0, 0.1),
  numeric(2000L)
)
d_crop <- decide_input_rate(
  yield_draws, rates, price_grain = 300, price_input = 1.2,
  grounding = grounding_grounded()
)
d_crop
#> <decision> decided  [grounded]
#>   action : rate=175
#>   E[utility]: 1356
#>   candidates: 9 evaluated (method: expected_profit)

The full candidate ledger – every rate evaluated, feasible or not, with its expected profit – is available for inspection or a methods appendix rather than discarded once the maximiser has run.

Candidate ledger for the nitrogen-rate decision, every rate on the grid.
Rate (kg N/ha) Expected profit (AUD/ha) Feasible
0 900 TRUE
25 1070 TRUE
50 1188 TRUE
75 1265 TRUE
100 1314 TRUE
125 1342 TRUE
150 1353 TRUE
175 1356 TRUE
200 1347 TRUE 
ledger_df <- d_crop@candidates
ledger_df$point_type <- ifelse(
  ledger_df$action == d_crop@action, "chosen", "evaluated"
)
ggplot2::ggplot(ledger_df, ggplot2::aes(x = action, y = expected_utility)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = point_type), size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = d_crop@action, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_d(name = NULL, end = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Nitrogen rate (kg N/ha)", y = "Expected profit (AUD/ha)",
    title = "Candidate ledger: nitrogen rate"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Expected profit against candidate nitrogen rate. The curve rises steeply at low rates, where nitrogen is well below the point of diminishing yield response, then flattens as the input cost catches up with the marginal yield gain; the chosen rate (marked) sits at the turning point, not at the top of the grid.

The grounding firewall, applied to a nitrogen rate

The identical posterior, prices and candidate grid, but this time the yield evidence carries grounding_unverified() – not checked against an external authority, the Independent Oracle Principle default.

d_crop_ungrounded <- decide_input_rate(
  yield_draws, rates, price_grain = 300, price_input = 1.2,
  grounding = grounding_unverified()
)
d_crop_ungrounded
#> <decision> ABSTAINED (input_ungrounded)  [ungrounded]
#>   action : rate=0 (status quo) [ungrounded]
#>   candidates: 9 evaluated (method: expected_profit)

The same engine, a different domain: sizing a trading position

decide_position_size() routes through the identical core: given predictive draws of the next-period return, it chooses the fraction of capital that maximises expected log-growth E[log⁡(1+fr)]\mathrm{E}[\log(1 + f\,r)] over a grid capped at kelly_cap, subject to a hard one-period loss-quantile constraint.

returns <- rnorm(5000L, mean = 0.02, sd = 0.03)    # a small positive edge
d_trade <- decide_position_size(
  returns, capital = 1000, max_drawdown = 0.15,
  grounding = grounding_grounded()
)
d_trade
#> <decision> decided  [grounded]
#>   action : size=50.0% (=500)
#>   E[utility]: 0.01023
#>   candidates: 41 evaluated (method: kelly_log_growth_drawdown_capped)
d_trade@metadata$position                          # implied dollar position
#> [1] 500

With no edge, the grid maximiser is naturally flat – the engine does not manufacture a position where none is warranted.

flat <- decide_position_size(
  rnorm(5000L, mean = 0, sd = 0.03), capital = 1000, max_drawdown = 0.15,
  grounding = grounding_grounded()
)
flat@action                                        # 0: flat
#> [1] 0

And the capital firewall: the same return draws that produced a decided position above, now carrying grounding_unverified() – a price feed not checked against the exchange – force flat, regardless of how attractive the numbers look.

d_trade_ungrounded <- decide_position_size(
  returns, capital = 1000, max_drawdown = 0.15,
  grounding = grounding_unverified()
)
d_trade_ungrounded@abstained
#> [1] TRUE
d_trade_ungrounded@abstain_reason
#> [1] "input_ungrounded"

The pipeline tail: deciding from an upstream manifest

In an ORCHESTRA pipeline the yield posterior above is not assembled by hand – it arrives as an orchestra_manifest emitted by an upstream member (a PESTO ensemble inversion, a kernR causal test, a flexyBayes posterior). decide_rate_from_manifest() reads the predictive draws and the producer’s grounding token straight off the manifest and closes the loop into a decision. decideR does not depend on the contract package – the manifest is read through its public properties (outputs, metadata, summary), so the tail consumes any conforming producer rather than special-casing each one. In production the manifest is a real orchestra_manifest S7 object from the composition layer; a minimal S7 stand-in carrying the same public properties is built below to keep this vignette self-contained.

vignette_manifest <- S7::new_class(
  "vignette_manifest",
  properties = list(
    outputs         = S7::new_property(S7::class_any, default = NULL),
    metadata        = S7::new_property(S7::class_list, default = list()),
    summary         = S7::new_property(S7::class_any, default = NULL),
    run_id          = S7::new_property(S7::class_character, default = ""),
    emitter_package = S7::new_property(S7::class_character, default = "")
  )
)
m_grounded <- vignette_manifest(
  outputs = yield_draws,
  metadata = list(grounding = grounding_grounded()),
  run_id = "pesto-001", emitter_package = "PESTO"
)
m_ungrounded <- vignette_manifest(
  outputs = yield_draws,
  metadata = list(grounding = grounding_unverified()),
  run_id = "pesto-002", emitter_package = "PESTO"
)
d_tail <- decide_rate_from_manifest(
  m_grounded, rates = rates, price_grain = 300, price_input = 1.2
)
d_tail
#> <decision> decided  [grounded]
#>   action : 175
#>   E[utility]: 1356
#>   candidates: 9 evaluated (method: expected_profit)
d_tail@inputs$emitter_package      # provenance carried from the manifest
#> [1] "PESTO"

The grounding rides from the producer through the decision: a manifest whose payload carries grounding_unverified() forces the status quo, the same firewall applied at the pipeline boundary rather than inside a single call.

d_tail_ungrounded <- decide_rate_from_manifest(
  m_ungrounded, rates = rates, price_grain = 300, price_input = 1.2
)
d_tail_ungrounded@abstained
#> [1] TRUE

For a fully general tail – any candidate set, any utility – decide_from_manifest() is the function decide_rate_from_manifest() wraps.

A threshold-economics loss: grade-band payoffs

Many grain payoffs are not smooth in the quality they reward. A delivery is paid by grade: the price steps up as protein clears a milling threshold and again at a premium threshold. The value of an outcome depends on which band it falls in, not on its exact magnitude, so the decision is governed by the posterior probability of clearing each band, not by the posterior mean. grade_band_value() makes that step payoff a first-class, reusable loss: a value schedule with breakpoints.

protein_value <- grade_band_value(
  breaks = c(11.5, 13.0),            # milling and premium protein thresholds
  values = c(300, 360, 420)          # AUD/t: feed, milling, premium
)
protein_value
#> <grade_band_value> 3 bands
#>          band value
#>  [-Inf, 11.5)   300
#>    [11.5, 13)   360
#>     [13, Inf)   420

Nitrogen lifts grain protein with diminishing returns; the per-hectare value folds in a 5.5 t/ha yield, and nitrogen costs 1.3 per unit rate. A posterior over the base (zero-nitrogen) protein feeds the rate of greatest expected per-hectare value.

qshift <- function(rate, base_protein) {
  base_protein + 3.0 * (1 - exp(-rate / 50))    # protein response to nitrogen
}
yield <- 5.5
grain_value <- function(rate, base_protein) {
  yield * protein_value(qshift(rate, base_protein)) - 1.3 * rate
}

base_protein <- rnorm(4000L, mean = 10.6, sd = 0.5)
rates_n <- seq(0, 150, by = 15)
d_protein <- decide(
  base_protein, grain_value, candidates = rates_n,
  grounding = grounding_grounded(), safe_action = 0
)
d_protein
#> <decision> decided  [grounded]
#>   action : 120
#>   E[utility]: 2069
#>   candidates: 11 evaluated (method: expected_utility)
prot_best <- qshift(d_protein@action, base_protein)
p_milling <- mean(prot_best >= 11.5)
p_premium <- mean(prot_best >= 13.0)
c(`P(>=11.5 milling)` = p_milling, `P(>=13 premium)` = p_premium)
#> P(>=11.5 milling)   P(>=13 premium) 
#>           0.99975           0.74400
Candidate ledger for the grade-band nitrogen decision.
Rate (kg N/ha) Expected value (AUD/ha) Feasible
0 1662 TRUE
15 1767 TRUE
30 1888 TRUE
45 1946 TRUE
60 1989 TRUE
75 2032 TRUE
90 2059 TRUE
105 2068 TRUE
120 2069 TRUE
135 2065 TRUE
150 2055 TRUE 
breaks <- attr(protein_value, "breaks")
values <- attr(protein_value, "values")
band_x <- c(min(prot_best) - 0.5, breaks, max(prot_best) + 0.5)
dens <- density(prot_best)
scale_k <- diff(range(values)) / max(dens$y)

plot_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    x = band_x, y = c(values, values[length(values)]),
    series = "grade-band value (AUD/t)", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    x = dens$x, y = dens$y * scale_k + min(values),
    series = "posterior density of protein", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)
ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = series)) +
  ggplot2::geom_step(
    data = plot_df[plot_df$series == "grade-band value (AUD/t)", ],
    direction = "hv", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = plot_df[plot_df$series == "posterior density of protein", ],
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = breaks, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_d(name = NULL, end = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Grade-band value (AUD/t)",
    sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(
      ~ (. - min(values)) / scale_k, name = "Posterior density of protein"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Protein (%)",
    title = "Grade-band schedule and posterior at chosen rate"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

The grade-band step schedule (blue, left axis) against protein, with the posterior density of protein at the chosen nitrogen rate overlaid (orange, right axis). Most of the posterior mass sits at or past the milling step and well into the premium band, which is why the engine pays for the nitrogen: it is buying probability of clearing a step, not moving the mean protein a little.

Read

The nitrogen-rate decision settles on 175 kg N/ha, at an expected profit of 1356 AUD/ha – an interior point of the nine-rate grid, short of the 200 kg N/ha ceiling, because beyond it the marginal yield response no longer covers the input cost. The figure makes the same point visually: the chosen rate sits at the turning point of the expected-profit curve, not at an extreme of it, and every rejected candidate stays visible in the ledger above it rather than being discarded once the maximiser has run.

The firewall changes nothing about the posterior or the prices, only the grounding token, and that alone is enough to move the decision: d_crop_ungrounded abstains (abstained is TRUE) with reason input_ungrounded, returns to the status-quo rate of 0 kg N/ha, and its action label is suffixed ungrounded so the caveat travels with the number wherever it is printed. No profit figure is quoted for a rate the evidence does not support.

The trading decision picks a 50% position ($500 of the $1000 capital base) on a small positive edge – exactly the kelly_cap ceiling of 50%, so the binding constraint here is the fractional-Kelly cap rather than the drawdown guard. With no edge the same engine settles on 0: a zero-edge return series gives the maximiser nothing to buy. Grounding the identical return draws as ungrounded reproduces the nitrogen firewall in the trading domain: d_trade_ungrounded abstains (TRUE) for the same reason, input_ungrounded, forcing flat regardless of how attractive the draws look.

The manifest tail reproduces the hand-assembled nitrogen decision exactly – d_tail@action is 175, matching d_crop@action – because decide_rate_from_manifest() reads the identical draws and the identical grounding token, only through the manifest’s public properties rather than by hand. Its inputs$emitter_package records PESTO, the provenance carried across the pipeline boundary. Swapping the manifest’s grounding to ungrounded abstains the tail (TRUE) exactly as the hand-assembled call did: the firewall is enforced at the boundary of the pipeline, not only inside a single function call.

The grade-band decision applies 120 kg N/ha of the 150 kg N/ha grid – enough to be certain of clearing the milling threshold (P(>=11.5 milling) is 100%) and to clear the premium threshold on 74% of the posterior, but not so much that the nitrogen cost outruns the extra premium. The figure shows why: most of the posterior density of protein at the chosen rate sits at or past the milling step and well into the premium band, so the engine is buying probability of clearing a step rather than nudging the mean protein a fraction of a percentage point.

Limits

Every posterior in this vignette is synthetic – a diminishing-returns nitrogen response, a Gaussian return series, a shifted protein response – chosen to keep the vignette fast and self-contained, not fitted to a field trial or a live price feed; a real PESTO inversion or kernR causal test would supply the actual posterior these examples stand in for. The grounding token is set directly by the caller in every example here, by hand, with grounding_grounded() or grounding_unverified(); decideR performs no verification step of its own. Establishing that a fact has actually been checked against the external authority that owns it is the job of the upstream producer, and decideR’s contribution is solely to combine that provenance worst-case and abstain when the combined label is not grounded. The trading position’s max_drawdown guard is a hard one-period loss-quantile constraint, not a multi-period peak-to-trough drawdown; a decision made period by period under this guard is not equivalent to a backtested trading strategy over a path. The low_ess trigger is opt-in and is not exercised anywhere in this vignette, since no call here supplies min_ess; decisive_prob is left at its default of 0.6 throughout, and a different threshold would move exactly which near-tie candidates abstain as insufficient_evidence, a sensitivity not explored here. The value-of-information verbs (decide_evpi(), decide_evsi()) and the benefit-cost verbs (decide_bcr(), bcr_crrdc()) added since this vignette was first written are not demonstrated here; see What to read next. Every decision above is a single static candidate scan, not a sequential or dynamic decision problem.

What to read next

From an inference result to a grain plan, grainPlan’s vignette, is the grain-specific decision orchestrator built directly on decideR’s manifest tail – it carries the pipeline demonstrated above through to a practitioner-facing recommendation. The package’s own reference pages for decide_evpi(), decide_evsi(), decide_bcr() and bcr_crrdc() cover the value-of-information and CRRDC-guideline benefit-cost verbs this vignette does not exercise; NEWS.md records the audit findings each of them closed.

Reproduce

Seed 1 for every random draw in this vignette, set once before the first chunk runs. Package versions follow.
